hypotheses.reasoning: The fault originates at the external translation API (https://api.translate.example/v2/translate), which catalog-svc calls synchronously while serving /products/batch. Latency first appears at #168 (20:43:23, 4784ms vs 2000ms soft threshold), then worsens at #171 (11950ms). From #181 onward, calls fail only after the 30000ms timeout (#181, #184, #199), so the dependency is hanging rather than failing fast. Before 20:43 every /products/batch call completed in roughly 20-85ms, and the failure began after the translation latency started climbing. Downstream, search-api's catalog calls time out at 30s (#182, #185, #200), its connection pool to catalog-svc saturates (#198, #210), and pool checkout times out (#221). web-bff then returns GET /search 503s (#201, #205, #213, #223, #227, #229, #240). Those 5xx lines and the pool saturation are symptoms and are not cited as evidence of the cause. Catalog-db, redis, and index-worker show no errors, which rules them out as the origin. An external outage is the main alternative, but the slow-then-hang pattern points to dependency_timeout rather than a fast-fail outage.

The translation API could be fully down rather than just slow. The timeouts at #181, #184, and #199 are consistent with this, but the earlier slow-call warnings (#168, #171) suggest degradation before failure, which fits a hang better than an outage.

verdict.recommendedAction: Mitigate the hang on the translation dependency: add or tighten a client timeout and circuit breaker on catalog-svc's translation calls (the 30s timeout is far too long for a synchronous request path), and fall back to untranslated or cached product text when translation is unavailable. Raise or bound the search-api to catalog-svc pool so it cannot queue indefinitely. Engage the translation provider or its status page to confirm the degradation, and check whether translation needs to be on the synchronous /products/batch path at all.
